title: MTU mismatch on peered dedicated clusters causing fragmentation blackhole -> DNS fallback and transient tenant crossover
creator: Maya Chen
description: Production incident: a subset of Dedicated customers experienced intermittent DNS resolution failures and, in one reported case, cross-tenant TCP handshake attempts during high-throughput bursts across VPC peering. Root cause traced to a path MTU mismatch introduced by transit gateway configuration in a customer peering path combined with fragmented UDP DNS responses being dropped by an overlay dataplane. This ticket covers the investigation, workaround rollouts, permanent fix, and postmortem actions.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-24 between 17:32-18:07 UTC, three dedicated tenants in us-west-2 reported timeouts resolving internal platform hostnames. During burst traffic from those tenants, some nodes observed repeated ICMP 'Fragmentation needed' messages from a downstream Transit GW. The dataplane had DF-handling that dropped fragmented UDP replies from the authoritative resolver; affected client libraries retried against public resolvers, which in one support case returned stale records and led to a transient connection attempt to an IP from another tenant's NAT pool. No data exfiltration confirmed. Customer impact included failed API calls and elevated latency for embeddings/generation requests.
timeline: 2026-02-24T17:32Z - First alert from Customer A via support (timeouts for internal DNS).
2026-02-24T17:38Z - PagerDuty triggered on elevated DNS error rate for dedicated cluster dc-usw2-09.
2026-02-24T17:45Z - Initial mitigation: applied per-cluster iptables rule to accept large UDP fragments and temporarily lower MTU on overlay interface to 1400 on affected hosts.
2026-02-24T18:02Z - Symptoms subsided for Customer A; additional customers B and C reported similar issues; mitigation rolled to all hosts in dc-usw2-09.

2026-02-25T09:10Z - Root cause analysis started with packet captures and control-plane config review; discovered inconsistent MTU advertised by customer-managed transit gateway and missing PMTU blackhole telemetry in our dataplane.
2026-02-26T11:40Z - Patch authored to ensure overlay (geneve) path-MTU discovery and to gracefully handle fragmented UDP DNS responses in our UDP proxy; PR opened.
2026-03-01T14:25Z - Patch merged and rolled out to runtime-1.22 for dedicated clusters; post-deploy validation completed.
2026-03-03T16:00Z - Postmortem reviewed with infra, networking, and support; action items agreed and ticket closed.
root_cause: A customer-side Transit Gateway was configured with a lower effective MTU (1476) but our overlay nodes were still using the default 1500 MTU. Large DNS responses (DNSSEC/EDNS enabled responses > 512 bytes) triggered fragmentation. Our overlay dataplane (Geneve encapsulation) did not surface PMTU/ICMP 'fragmentation needed' signals reliably to the kernel path and additionally had a UDP proxy path that dropped out-of-order/fragmented DNS UDP replies. The combination led to DNS timeouts; some clients fell back to public resolvers causing stale mapping exposure. Operationally, we lacked a robust PMTU blackhole detection and an automated mitigation path for peered transit MTU mismatches.
fix_summary: 1) Immediate mitigation: lowered overlay MTU to 1400 on affected nodes and updated iptables to accept fragmented UDP responses while investigation proceeded. 2) Short-term code change: made UDP proxy tolerant to fragmented DNS replies by reassembling fragments in userland and falling back to TCP for large DNS answers. 3) Long-term fix: added PMTU probing and detection in the dataplane control loop with automatic overlay MTU alignment when a peered path advertises lower MTU or when repeated ICMP PMTU messages are observed. Also updated onboarding docs to include transit-gateway MTU checks for customer-managed peering.
deploy_record: runtime-1.22 rollout: staged to canary (dc-usw2-01) 2026-02-28, degraded metrics monitored; full roll 2026-03-01 completed by 20:00 UTC. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-infra/internal/d/peering/peering-pmtu?orgId=1
rollback_plan: If new PMTU handling causes instability, revert the runtime-1.22 overlay MTU changes while keeping the UDP-reassembly proxy enabled. Revert PR #5892 via standard revert PR and run quick acceptance on canary before re-rolling. Primary mitigation (iptables + MTU 1400) can be reapplied cluster-wide as emergency stop-gap.
postmortem_actions: Add PMTU blackhole detection and alerting (ENG task) - estimate 5 points
Enhance UDP proxy to always attempt TCP fallback for large DNS answers and add tests for fragmented UDP responses - estimate 3 points
Update Dedicated peering onboarding checklist to include MTU verification and provide a customer-run script - ops task

Create a runbook for DNS failures caused by peering (support + SRE) and automate emergency MTU/iptables mitigation via orchestration - runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/peering-dns-runbook
Add synthetic tests in canary that exercise large DNS responses and PMTU scenarios (CI/networks)
notes: This incident surfaced an intersection bug between customer-configured network elements and our overlay assumptions. No confirmed data leak or cross-tenant data plane compromise beyond a single attempted TCP connection observed in logs. Legal/compliance notified; CSP/enterprise customers on impacted clusters offered credits and detailed RCA. Support ticket references: SUP-11876, SUP-11881, SUP-11890.
